title: The Last Wreck
premise: Ada Almeida has spent seven years flying medicine and rumors into the interior, keeping her distance from the river salvage crew she once belonged to — and from the wreck of the Corvina, the ship her father died trying to claim. When old rival Marcus Vey hires her crew for a monsoon-season run upriver, she discovers he's found the Corvina's manifest and means to strip it before the flood season seals the gorge forever. Betrayed mid-river by Vey's hired muscle, Ada, her mechanic Juno, and a stranger named Elias — who turns out to be the illegitimate son of the Corvina's owner — must survive the monsoon in a leaking boat, outmaneuver Vey's armed salvage team, and decide whether the inheritance they're chasing is gold or justice. In the climax, Ada deliberately scuttles the recovered treasure into the gorge rather than let Vey take it, forcing him to choose between drowning for wealth or living empty-handed; the epilogue finds her testifying to a coastal tribunal that grants the wreck's estate to Elias, while Ada finally measures life in years again.
about_author: Xanthe Galloway is the pen name of a former bush-strip radio operator who spent a decade in remote river settlements before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who live where the law arrives late, if at all.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She flies a medevac run through storm-fringed valleys, establishing her rhythm of avoidance: no attachments, no rivers, no talk of the Corvina. A letter waiting at the strip bears a name she hasn't spoken in seven years. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath competent calm.

chapters.title: The Letter from Vey
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Marcus Vey offers triple pay for a monsoon-season cargo run upriver — no questions, no manifests. Her mechanic Juno urges refusal; their debts argue otherwise. Ada signs, telling herself it's just freight. Emotional beat: the first compromise, rationalized.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ada's POV. Seven years earlier: the Corvina expedition, her father's death in the gorge, the oath the surviving crew swore never to return. The reader learns what Vey's job really is. Emotional beat: grief hardened into rule.

chapters.title: Loading the Leech
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Preparations aboard their aging river boat, the Leech; crates heavier than any medicine, a hired deckhand who won't give his name — Elias. Juno notices Vey's men counting rifles, not cargo. Emotional beat: creeping dread.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ascent through narrowing gorges; beauty and menace braided together. Elias proves eerily knowledgeable about the river's dead reaches. First exchange of barbed trust between him and Ada. Emotional beat: watchful attraction.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He reveals himself: son of the Corvina's owner, holder of half a manifest, cheated of his inheritance by Vey's forged papers. He didn't hire them — he stowed toward the same goal. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Vey's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. At the forward camp, we see his ledger-mind: crews as costs, Ada as an asset with one sentimental flaw. He orders the Leech's fuel siphoned. Emotional beat: cold competence curdling into corruption.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Dawn: the Leech is dry, the crew marooned above the falls as the monsoon's first wall of rain arrives. Vey's men are gone upstream with the gear. Emotional beat: betrayal's sick drop.

chapters.title: Rain Like Iron
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Survival improvisation: patching the hull, rigging a still, Elias navigating by drowned landmarks only he seems to know. The three become a reluctant unit. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in misery.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They shelter in a settlement abandoned when the dam schemes came — including the grave of the man who witnessed the forged will. Elias reads his father's letters aloud. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as story, not gold.

chapters.title: Rafting the Gorge
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A brutal night passage through the same gorge that killed Ada's father; she steers where he died, closing a circle. They lose half their supplies but gain the shortcut ahead of Vey. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into mastery.

chapters.title: The Corvina's Ribs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They reach the wreck first — visible now in low water, cargo hold intact. Inside: not bullion alone but documents proving the theft of Elias's birthright. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by greed's temptation.

chapters.title: Juno's Bargain
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Tempted by a private cut, Juno nearly signals Vey's approaching launch, then burns the signal instead and confesses. Trust survives its hardest test. Emotional beat: shame redeemed by honesty.

chapters.title: Vey Arrives
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. His armed team takes the wreck site; he offers Ada partnership, invoking her father's ambition. She refuses; he orders them held for the monsoon to dispose of. Emotional beat: the villain's sincere, corrupting logic.

chapters.title: Held Above the Waterline
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Captives in a collapsing camp; Elias plays the obedient heir, feeding Vey false coordinates for the document cache. Small rebellions accumulate. Emotional beat: patience as resistance.

chapters.title: The River Rises
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The monsoon peaks; the gorge begins to drown the wreck permanently. Escape window measured in hours. Juno sabotages Vey's winch; the three slip into the flood. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Scuttling
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cornered on the wreck itself, Ada makes her choice: she opens the Corvina's seams, sending the treasure into the gorge rather than letting Vey haul it out. Vey dives after it against all sense. Emotional beat: sacrifice as verdict.

chapters.title: What Vey Chose
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Underwater, tangled, he surfaces empty as the Corvina's last ribs fold. His crew deserts; his ledger finally balances to nothing. Emotional beat: power revealed as hunger that devours its host.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The battered trio rides the flood to the coast, carrying the salvaged documents sealed in oilcloth. Quiet scenes of aftermath — injuries, jokes, the strange lightness of having chosen rightly. Emotional beat: exhausted grace.

chapters.title: The Tribunal at Port Meridian
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Justice inside the law at last: testimony, the forged will exposed, the estate adjudicated. Vey, ruined, watches from the gallery. Elias wins the name and lands he was denied. Emotional beat: vindication without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elias offers her a share and a partnership; she accepts neither money nor ground, but something better — a reason to stay in one place awhile. She visits her father's grave with the news. Emotional beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, coda. One year later: Ada flies the medicine run again, but keeps a garden, keeps friends, keeps Sundays. A new letter arrives bearing a stranger's plea — and she reads it slowly, unhurried. Emotional beat: peace earned, adventure welcomed on her own terms.
